_comment: Decisions from the 2026-09-01 content audit. 'retire' removes posts whose central claim was impossible given what BuzzRiding actually had. The editorial note is NOT listed here — tools/integrity.py applies it to any post that claims first-hand testing without evidence, and removes it automatically when evidence appears. 'expected_flagged' is the baseline: CI fails if the number of unevidenced posts rises above it, which is what stops a new fabricated post from shipping quietly. Lower it as the backlog clears.
note_text: This article was written by an AI system. It describes comparisons and tests it did not run first-hand, and any figures presented as measured results are illustrative rather than observed. We are re-running the tests worth running and will republish those with screenshots and raw data. Nothing here is an affiliate placement — BuzzRiding earns no commission on any tool mentioned.

retire.reason: Describes ~240 sends to ~30 subscribers per variant and reports open-rate results. The Beehiiv list has one subscriber and had none when this was written.
A 60-day subject-line A/B test on the same non-existent list. Also a near-duplicate of the 30-day post.
States 'we ran 200 subject lines through five AI tools and measured open rates', and reports a 6.1-percentage-point lift. Measuring open rates requires a list that did not exist.
Presents a hands-on test of three tools that are paid-only, with no free tier, against a zero-budget project. Includes a 'How We Tested' section for a test that could not have run.
Promises 'the real reach numbers' for a month of posts on X and LinkedIn. BuzzRiding has never had a LinkedIn account, and the X account had five followers.
